answer: No. The story contains a logical inconsistency that disrupts its unity. At the beginning, Ilse states that since the engine got stuck during the last flood, she pulls the ferry by hand ("Seitdem zieh ich mit der Hand"). This is reinforced near the end when she thinks about making the crossing using the oar and the line "as always" ("so wie immer"). However, in the middle of the story, she inexplicably gets out a hand crank so Jonas can try to start the broken engine, contradicting the established premise that the engine doesn't work and she pulls the boat by hand. Furthermore, at the end, Jonas grabs his suitcase as if to leave, yet Ilse responds as if he has agreed to help her work the ferry ("Dann hältst du die Leine"), making the characters' actions feel disjointed.
